title.narrative: Sw Council of Churches OPT CAP 2013

description.narrative: Syftet med programmet är att minska övergrepen mot de mänskliga rättigheterna och internationell humanitär lag i Palestina och Israel. Detta genom ett ekumeniskt följeslagare program där personer från hela världen kommer för att stödja civilt fredsskapande genom icke-vålds metoder.

Through the Ecumenical Accompaniment Programme in Palestine and Israel (EAPPI), people from different parts of the world come as ecumenical accompaniers to Palestine and Israel, to support, with non-violent means, through civilian peacekeeping. The overall objective of the programme is to decrease violations of human rights and international humanitarian law (IHL) in Palestine and Israel.

General question: Results related to the intended outcome 2015Question: Summarise results related to the intended outcome (this information will be sent to Open Aid)Answer: The overall objective of the programme is to decrease violations of human rights (HR) and international humanitarian law (IHL) in Palestine and Israel. Based on the 2014 results matrix, the following has been reported as results of the Sida support: 1. Improved access and freedom of movement for civilians (girls, boys, women and men), at the monitored locations. Improved access to land for farmers and herders, in areas where EAPPI provide protective presence, thus, reduced threat of displacement. Decreased number of violent acts and harassment towards the people accompanied; girls, boys, women and men, in particular in areas close to settlements and closed military zones, checkpoints and agricultural gates where EAPPI provides targeted protective presence. Increased awareness of HR and IHL among local people, applicable in their daily lives. 2. EAPPI has cooperated with several Israeli and Palestinian human rights organisations that advocate for peace, human rights and protection of civilians under IHL. 3. EAPPI has been contributing to the Humanitarian Bulletin, the monthly update on the humanitarian situation in Palestine by UNOCHA and disseminates its reports within the communities, also EAPPI works with OCHA, OHCHR, ICRC. In 2014 EAPPI was again central in the coordination of the protective presence during the olive harvest together with OCHA and the UN Protection Cluster.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
